newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slide back in sluggish turnover.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slide back in sluggish turnover.

text.p: Egyptian share prices on Tuesday drifted back into the down trend that has gripped the market for days and turnover slipped to its lowest since December 1996.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index fell 1.97 points to close at 355.54 points, after losing the 0.05 percent it had gained on Monday. Turnover was a paltry 28.6 million pounds ($8.42), its lowest level since December 1.

"The market is steady and it will remain this way for a while. We need more money inflows and new deals," said broker Sherif Cararah of EFG Hermes. "Nothing special is happening. Buyers are trickling in very slowly."

Cement and milling stocks remained active on Tuesday but unfamiliar stocks Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries and Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries also made it into the list of the day's most active firms.

Both firms are among 16 identified by the International Finance Corporation EG/IFC as part of its index of the most active firms on the bourse. Eipico rose 0.25 pounds to 210.25 in 1.49 million pounds worth of trade while Abu Qir traded shares worth 1.53 million but ended unchanged at 82.
"The interest in Eipico is understandable. It is certainly the blue chip of the pharmaceutical sector and it's very attractive at this price," said Cararah.

Helwan Portland Cement was the most active in its sector and during the day, rising 0.25 pounds to 72.25 after turnover worth 2.1 million pounds. Suez Cement was a close second in terms of trading volume and climbed 0.4 to 67.8 pounds.
In the milling sector, Upper Egypt Flour Mills was the most traded but shares fell 0.5 to 79 pounds. East Delta Flour Mills also attracted investors and the stock rose 0.9 to 65 pounds.
Banks were also popular but the most active ended lower. Commercial International Bank (CIB) slipped 0.34 to 72.66 and the Export Development Bank of Egypt fell 3 pounds to 437.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 493.09 points from 496.30 and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms slipped to 261.28 from 262.60 points.
Out of the 101 shares traded, 29 rose, 43 fell while 29 ended unchanged.
